name: Green
story: Green is the color computing actually lived in, but not as #00FF00. It came as three physical materials, and each one becomes a ground. PHOSPHOR (dark) is the unlit, tinted faceplate of a monochrome CRT with P1 phosphor text glowing on it. SOLDERMASK (mid) is the green lacquer on a circuit board, with white silkscreen legends and ENIG gold pads. GREENBAR (light) is continuous-form line-printer paper, printed in near-black ribbon ink. Screen, board and paper: the whole palette stays inside computing's own history. Hue is measured, not guessed. The approximate CIE 1931 chromaticity of P1 (zinc orthosilicate:Mn, x 0.218 / y 0.712) converts to OKLCH hue 150.6. Every green uses that hue, with chroma capped at 0.135, so the palette reads as phosphor without the neon. The accent is the historical rival, the amber monitor. P3 amber (x 0.523 / y 0.469) gives hue 77.7, and it marks trust boundaries, the sink and finding chip1 on every ground: bright amber on the tube, ENIG gold on the board, ochre ink on paper. The three tape chips follow the three phosphor colors of that era's terminals (DEC's VT220 was sold with white, green or amber tubes): chip1 is amber, chip2 is P1 green (the one place chroma rises, so findings stand out), and chip3 uses P4 white's cool hue (235.1: a cool white on the tube, tin/HASL on the board, slate ribbon ink on paper). The chips stay clearly apart, with CIEDE2000 ΔE of 36.1/32.6/33.2 on PHOSPHOR, 26.2/27.5/24.0 on SOLDERMASK and 36.5/36.9/35.6 on GREENBAR. Amber against green is the pair that red-green dichromats confuse. Under Machado 2009 simulation every chip pair stays at ΔE00 10 or more (worst case: PHOSPHOR 10.3 protan, SOLDERMASK 10.1 protan, GREENBAR 10.9 deutan). To reach that, only the green chip moved, and only in lightness: PHOSPHOR chip2 went from #5DBC77 to #47A764, and SOLDERMASK chip2 = angle went from #94DBA4 to #A0E7B0. The amber anchor was left untouched. Role reuse follows purple so the renderer can swap palettes directly. PHOSPHOR matches ANILINE: frame=rule, text=diag, text2=data, tb=sink=chip1. SOLDERMASK matches INDIGO: data=tb=sink=chip1 in gold, angle=chip2. GREENBAR matches DITTO: text=diag, text2=data, tb=sink=chip1. The minor rgba is the major color at purple's alpha (.40/.45/.34), and grid contrast was set to purple's levels (major 2.2/2.5/2.3). This avoids the cliché because there is no matrix rain, no glow, no black #000 and no pure #0F0. It is flat, low-chroma material color with a documented source, and the amber counterpoint adds warmth. All ratios come from a WCAG 2.x relative-luminance script (the rgba minor is composited over bg first). Every text role is at least 5.05:1 and every meaningful mark at least 3.81:1. Test renders through the real render_desktop.py build() look right on all three grounds.
